title: Mini-case: LogiFlow warehouses
text: LogiFlow runs 14 e-commerce warehouses in Germany and Poland. Pickers wear scanners that track every movement; the system ranks them daily and pays a bonus per item picked. Job descriptions are narrow, and team leaders spend most of their time checking dashboards.

Productivity is high, but annual staff turnover is 48 %, sick leave is rising, and a new automation project needs experienced employees to suggest process improvements – almost nobody does. The works council complains about constant surveillance, and local communities report difficulties hiring for LogiFlow's night shifts.

title: Mini-case: copying Google's HR
text: A 300-employee family-owned manufacturer of industrial valves in rural Austria hires a new CEO from a tech firm. She wants to introduce “Google-style” HR: unlimited holidays, a 20 % time rule for own projects, peer-based ratings and stock options. The workforce is long-tenured, partly unionized, and production runs in shifts with strict safety rules.
